_doc: Editorial config for the three data tables on /benchmarks/. The engine-comparison table and the scenario picker pull their numeric values from scalability_results.json (the raw engine-bench output); the storage table pulls its own from pmtiles_results.json. This file supplies display labels, captions, column specs and the scenario picker's commentary. Speed-cell templates: {throughput}, {mp}, {memory} are substituted from the matching engine's row at the showcase MP. Each table may carry an optional column_sizing block to override the default first-column auto-sizing rule (see _column_sizing_doc below). Cells with no measurement behind them are handled by the pending convention (see _pending_doc below).
_column_sizing_doc: Default first-column auto-sizing rule used by every table. The renderer measures each first-column cell at single-line max-content width; if that width exceeds threshold_ratio × the resulting other-column width, the first column is capped at cap_ratio × the other-column width and its cells wrap. Override per-table by placing a `column_sizing` block inside engine_table, scenario_table or storage_table.
_pending_doc: There is no pending flag anywhere in the data, and the renderer reads none. A metric is pending when its value is null, full stop, and that is the whole signal: fmt() prints the em dash it already prints for an absent metric, and a table row every one of whose metric cells came back null is marked pending. Pending is per row, never per engine or per storage backend, so filling one row in changes exactly that row. A pending row gets `pending_marker` beside its label and the [data-bench-note] paragraph under that same table is filled from `pending_note` and un-hidden; both are keyed on the table, and the renderer suppresses the marker entirely when the table has no note element to point at. Filling the nulls clears the marker and hides the note with no edit to this file. It does NOT update the static fallback rows in index.html, which are the JS-off copy of the same cells: benchmarks/tools/bench-drift.js is the gate that catches those, and it has to be run and satisfied in the same change.

engine_table._showcase_mp_target_doc: Renders the bench row whose megapixel count is closest to this target. Anchors the showcase numbers to the size the surrounding prose discusses, so the table doesn't drift onto a larger benchmarked size whenever the bench grid grows. Update both this value and the prose in benchmarks.html together if you want a different size.

_storage_export_fields_doc: Every key pmtiles_results.json rows carry, in the order the producer emits them: width, height, megapixels, tile_size, engine, concurrency, wall_time_ms, tracked_memory_mb, peak_rss_mb, tiles_produced, tiles_per_second, tiles_per_second_per_mb, resource_cost, scenario, storage, profile, output_bytes, filesystem_entries, tile_bytes_returned, p50_latency_us, p99_latency_us. Nullable: tracked_memory_mb, output_bytes and filesystem_entries are null on a read row, and tile_bytes_returned, p50_latency_us and p99_latency_us are null on a generation row. Nothing is ever 0 to mean absent. `profile` is the harness's sweep label ("ci" or "large") and this renderer does not read it; it is listed here so the next person does not think it appeared from nowhere. The renderer reads keys by name, so a key it does not know is carried harmlessly.
_storage_table_doc: Fed by pmtiles_results.json, which is a separate export from a separate harness and has nothing to do with scalability_results.json. Storage is an axis crossed with the engines rather than a fifth engine, so it gets its own table and its own columns: the engine table has no home for output_bytes, filesystem_entries or a per-lookup latency. Rows in that export are NOT unique on (engine, megapixels) — one pyramid carries a generation row and five read rows — so every lookup here keys on (storage, width, height, tile_size, scenario, concurrency) and each column names the scenario it reads. A lookup that matches more than one row returns nothing rather than the first match, because publishing a read row's wall time in a generation column is exactly the failure this shape is guarding against. Two columns may share a `key` and differ only in `scenario` (the cold and the random read both report p50_latency_us), so a column is identified by the pair and never by its key alone.

storage_table.pending_note: † The storage measurements are pending. This table reads its own export, pmtiles_results.json, written by the PMTiles benchmark suite in libviprs#993 rather than by the engine bench above. Every cell stays empty until that export lands here, because a guessed figure on a benchmarks page is a figure somebody quotes back. The grid, the backends and the columns are the ones that suite measures; only the numbers are outstanding.
